speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) in relation to construction noise near residential estates, how is compliance with noise thresholds enforced and how frequently is it monitored; (b) how are prolonged duration and cumulative exposure to such noise factored into enforcement measures; and (c) whether noise thresholds will be reviewed, including the use of psycho-acoustic factors such as sharpness and roughness of sound.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: Residents in Tampines living near the long-running Loyang Viaduct construction have reported prolonged stress from construction noise.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: So, given that sounds of similar decibel levels can differ in perceived loudness and distress, does the Ministry consider the use of psycho-acoustic factors, such as sharpness and roughness, in the review of thresholds?

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And another supplementary question would be what are the penalties when construction sites exceed noise thresholds?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to review our stance as well as take reference from the WHO with respect to what are the factors of sound that we take into account when enforcing the framework.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are different ways in which we do this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The requirement for monitoring itself is a burden placed on the site operator, potentially requiring closed circuit television (CCTV), continuous real time monitoring.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Thereafter, there are composition sums, depending on the circumstances of the case and the court findings.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Similar to the hon Member, Dr Chen, I also receive feedback from residents of RiverEdge, a condominium that is situated in Tanjong Rhu.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The lived experience on the ground appears to differ materially from what average equivalent continuous sound level (LEq) measurements suggest, with the Tanjong Rhu Build-To-Order construction site located less than 150 metres of existing residential block, residents have informed me that these repeated short bursts of intense construction noise that are technically compliant when averaged over five minutes – but nonetheless, they are quite disruptive.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: So, I have two questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: In such close proximity situations, how does NEA assess whether the current averaging based approach adequately reflects the actual disturbance experienced by the residents?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: And will the Ministry consider using Lmax instead in assessing compliance and addressing residents' complaints?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, we will consider and review how to best provide the correct supervision, regulatory framework and enforcement.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, there is a balance that we need to strike for different types of sound: persistent recurrent, repeated sharp bursts, as Ms Gho has pointed out.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And this is also something that is under study internationally.
